search_space._comment_mode: 'mode' is itself an optimized hyperparameter: each trial samples whether to run 'rag' or 'agentic', then only that mode's sub-space below is sampled. Restrict choices to a single mode (e.g. ["rag"]) to optimize just that mode instead.

_comment_search_space: One sub-space per mode; only the one matching a trial's sampled mode is used for that trial. Same per-parameter spec syntax either way: 'int'/'float' need 'low'/'high' (float accepts an optional 'log': true for log-scale sampling); 'bool' needs nothing else.
_comment_fixed_params: Per-mode hyperparameters passed to every trial of that mode but never sampled (e.g. pin top_n while optimizing everything else in rag). Must not overlap with that mode's search_space keys.
_comment_n_trials: Number of configurations Optuna will try. With Bayesian optimization (TPE), 30-50 trials is usually enough to clearly beat random/grid search on a search space this size.
_comment_timeout_seconds: Optional wall-clock budget for the whole study (stops launching new trials once exceeded). null = no limit, only n_trials governs the budget.
_comment_questions_limit: Cap the number of dataset questions evaluated per trial. Useful to dry-run/debug the optimizer itself quickly; set to null to use the full 94-question dataset for real runs.
_comment_workers: Threads used to evaluate questions of a SINGLE trial in parallel (same idea as benchmark.py --workers; -1 uses all CPUs). Each unit here is a full chatbot.py subprocess that reloads its own models from scratch (the RAG reranker alone is ~2-4GB of RAM) -- unlike a lightweight thread, so a high value can exhaust RAM and make the run appear to hang (or get OOM-killed) rather than actually deadlocking. Keep this modest (2-4) unless you've confirmed the machine has enough RAM for that many concurrent model loads, and keep it at 1 if the LLM endpoint enforces rate limits. Multiplies with n_jobs below (n_jobs x workers concurrent chatbot calls at once), so raise them one at a time.
_comment_n_jobs: Number of trials Optuna runs concurrently. Keep at 1 unless your LLM/chatbot backend can comfortably absorb several simultaneous full dataset evaluations at once.
_comment_dataset_shuffle_seed: dataset.json is grouped by module/topic, not shuffled, so evaluating only the first N questions of a pruned trial would be a biased, unrepresentative sample. The dataset is shuffled once with this seed and then reused in that same order for every trial, so pruning compares trials on equivalent partial samples. Set to null to keep the file's original order (not recommended if pruning is enabled).
_comment_storage: Optuna storage URL, e.g. 'sqlite:///studies/chatbot_hyperparameter_optimization.db'. Leave null to auto-generate a local SQLite file under evaluator/optimizer/studies/<study_name>.db. Re-running with the same study_name/storage resumes and adds trials to the same study instead of starting over — valuable since a full study can take hours.
_comment_pruning: A trial only becomes eligible for pruning after n_warmup_trials other trials have fully completed (so the pruner has something to compare against) AND after min_questions_before_pruning questions have been evaluated within that trial itself (so one unlucky early question can't kill an otherwise good config). From then on it is re-checked every interval_questions questions, and pruned only if its running average score falls below the given percentile of other trials at the same step — trials of both modes are compared together, which is exactly what lets a bad rag config lose out to a good agentic one (or vice versa). Set enabled to false to always run every trial through the full dataset.
_comment_final_validation: Each metric score is stochastic (LLM-graded), so the single best-value trial found during the search could just be lucky. After optimization, the top_k trials (ranked by Optuna's value, regardless of which mode they used) are each re-evaluated on the FULL dataset 'repeats' more times (no pruning) to report a mean +/- standard deviation per candidate and pick a genuinely robust winner rather than a noisy outlier.
